vulnerable_statements.reason: The report descriptor comes from the device, and its length (*rsize) is never checked. A short descriptor (fewer than 4 bytes) makes these reads go past the end of the buffer.
Reads offsets 115 and 116 without checking that *rsize >= 117. A malicious or malformed USB device can supply a shorter descriptor, which causes a slab out-of-bounds read.
Writes to offset 115 without checking the length, so a short descriptor allows an out-of-bounds write.
Writes to offset 116 without checking the length, so a short descriptor allows an out-of-bounds write.

suggested_fix: Check the descriptor length before touching any byte, e.g. `if (*rsize >= 117 && rdesc[2] == 0x09 && rdesc[3] == 0x02 && (rdesc[115] | rdesc[116] << 8) >= HID_MAX_USAGES)`. This keeps all reads and writes at offsets 2, 3, 115 and 116 inside the buffer the device supplied.
